editorial:
Imagine finding a giant, fluffy Yeti hiding on your apartment roof in Shanghai. That is exactly how this adventure begins, and it only gets more magical from there. You follow Yi, a determined teenager, along with her friends Jin and Peng, as they try to help a lost Yeti named Everest get back to his mountain home. Along the way, they dodge a wealthy collector and his team who want to capture the creature. The movie feels like a warm hug mixed with a road trip, packed with beautiful scenery, funny moments, and a lot of heart. It is the kind of film that makes you want to call your family afterward.

The animation is gorgeous, especially the sweeping shots of Chinese landscapes and glowing blueberries that light up the night. The pacing keeps things moving without feeling rushed, and the humor lands for both kids and adults. Some jokes are a bit predictable, and the villain is pretty standard, but the emotional beats more than make up for it. If you love heartfelt family adventures, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final act, Everest uses his magical powers to create a giant wave of flowers and light, helping the kids escape the collector. Yi realizes Everest needs to go home, and they reach the mountain together. Everest reunites with his Yeti family, and Yi finally plays her late father's violin at the peak, honoring his memory. The collector is left behind, and the friends head home changed. It is a sweet, emotional goodbye that ties everything together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt family adventures and beautiful animation.
